The counting lemma converts bounded numerator empirical measures to a sharp N(t)~C/t law, with the negative Fourier modes contributing a factor two. Weyl equidistribution holds under the stated independence and in every residue class for irrational a and rational b. Finite cosine sums yield exactly cotangent for even q and cosecant for odd q; x cot x and x csc x yield the strict comparisons and extrema. The n b half-integer condition gives the exact zero class. For b=2a an explicit |2u²-1| integral gives (16 sqrt(2)-8)/(3 pi²). Monotone inversion yields k s_k~C and the Schatten threshold; a self-contained checker performed 18153 finite corroboration assertions, with no finite experiment substituted for infinite proof.

value.rationale: This computes the natural exact weak-Schatten leading coefficient of a coherent two-exposure circle blur, directly governing the asymptotic number of recoverable modes. The interference factor generates a complete rational-denominator parity transition, sharp rational minimum and maximum, and positive-density spectral nullity precisely for even denominators. A dependent-irrational counterexample distinguishes rational independence from mere irrationality, preventing an incorrect uniform spectral approximation. The result answers an operator-theoretic blur problem not covered by the standard single boxcar or multiple separately observed channels; no unrelated parameter slice or unsupported inverse-risk theorem is asserted.
